answer: Cross-epoch behavioural mirror rule. Each identity's action vector from epoch N is stored and compared against its epoch N+1 behaviour; a genuine agent's activity tide should correlate across epochs on task-type and counterpart distributions. Sybil clusters reveal themselves because independently spawned identities cannot reproduce prior correlations, only imitate them shallowly. A falcon-weighted divergence score flags mismatches, and flagged identities lose routing priority plus a fixed revalidation deposit per identity.
